messages.content: i want to say my desk has less books now. is that the best way to say it?
fewer books is the word choice for a smaller number of books. you could say: my desk has fewer books on it now.
what if i am talking about the work of cleaning the desk?
then you could say less work. you can count books one by one. work in that sentence is not a number of objects.
say the difference more simply.
use fewer when you mean a smaller number of books. use less when you mean the cleaning will take less work.
so fewer books can mean less work?
it can in your example, if having fewer books makes the desk more simple to clean. one part is about a number of objects. the other part is about the cleaning you need to do.
give me one sentence with both fewer and less in it.
with fewer books on my desk, i have less work to do before i can use it.
what if i move the books to the floor and then have to clean that too?
then you may have fewer books on the desk without having less work in the whole room. moving the books can leave you with more cleaning in another place.
what does this mean: i will walk to the park unless there is rain?
the plan is to walk to the park, but rain could change that plan.
give me just the sentence about my plan again.
i will walk to the park unless there is rain.
does that mean i will still take that walk if there is rain?
no. the rain is the part that could stop or change the walk. you could say it more clearly this way: if there is rain, i will not take that walk.
can you explain the other part too?
if there is no rain, the plan you gave is to walk to the park. the part after unless gives the reason you would change that plan.
use only simple words and give the whole meaning again.
i plan to walk to the park. if there is rain, i will change that plan.
what if i want to go even when there is rain?
then unless there is rain would give the wrong meaning. you could say: i will walk to the park even if there is rain.
so one small word can change my plan?
yes. unless there is rain and even if there is rain give different information about what you will do.
my cousin says she does not read every day. can i tell my brother she never reads?
no. not reading every day is different from never reading. she may read on some days and not on other days.
if she reads on one day this week, would her sentence still be true?
yes. reading on one day would not mean she reads every day. it would also show that never reads is not right for that week.
what should i say if i only know her first sentence?
she does not read every day.
why not add that she reads on one day each week?
because that would be a new detail. she did not tell you how often she reads, only that it is not every day.
i want a sentence that does not sound as if reading is wrong.
my cousin does not read every day, but that does not mean she never reads.
could i also say she chooses every day herself?
no. that part was not in the information you gave. we only know that she does not read every day. there could be many reasons for that.
keep only what she told me.
she does not read every day.
should i put the picture in the letter before i close it?
if you want to send the picture with the letter, put it inside before closing the letter for sending.
i mean i wrote a letter, and i have a photo to send with it. i do not need a whole plan about sending it. just tell me the order.
understood. put the photo with the letter before you close it. that answers which of those two things goes first.
which one goes first: closing it or adding the photo?
adding the photo goes first.
can you answer that as a full sentence?
put the photo with the letter before you close it.
what if i already closed it and forgot the photo?
then the photo is still outside. you would need to find a way to put it with the letter before sending them together.
are you sure i forgot it just because it is outside?
no. that answer used your words that you forgot it. if you only said the photo was outside, i would not know why you left it there.
say that last answer more simply.
i used your words that you forgot the photo. being outside by itself would not tell me why it was there.
i have been listening to the same song all morning. my sister is tired of hearing it.
it sounds as if you enjoy it more than she does right now. can you listen in a way that does not make her hear it again?
i can go to another room. i do not want to stop playing it just because she does not want to hear it.
you do not have to change what you like. you can enjoy the song and also care about what your sister needs in the room you use together.
what if she says she does not like the song at all?
that may be how she feels about it. it does not mean you must have the same taste in music.
i want to answer without making the conversation feel hard for either of us.
you could say: i like this song, but i understand you have heard it enough today. i will listen in the other room.
give me just the message now, with no explanation.
i like this song, but i understand you have heard it enough today. i will listen in the other room.
what did we keep the same?
you still like the song. the change is where you listen, so your sister does not have to hear it again.
i drew a blue circle and a blue square. are they the same because both are blue?
they have the same color, but not the same shape. two things can be the same in one way and different in another.
say that in a shorter way.
they have the same color, but not the same shape.
if i make the circle red, what changes?
the color of the circle changes. the circle is still a circle unless you change its shape too.
what is still blue after that?
the square, if you did not change its color.
can you say the red one is a square now?
not from what you said. you changed the color of the circle, not its shape.
write a sentence about both pictures after my change.
there is a red circle and a blue square.
now i draw another picture of a circle, also red. how many red pictures do i have?
two red pictures.
use a full sentence.
you have two red pictures.
what did i keep the same while adding the new picture?
you did not say you changed the blue square or the first red circle. adding a new picture did not have to change either of those.
write a story about a woman finding a ticket at the station and giving it back to the person who lost it.

a woman was waiting at the station when she saw a ticket under a chair. she took it in her hand and looked around. a man near the door was looking through his things and looked worried. she asked if he had lost a ticket. he said yes and told her which train he was taking. she looked at the ticket to check whether it was the one he needed. when she knew it was right, she gave it back. he said thank you and put it away. they then went back to waiting.
tell that story again in fewer words.

a woman found a ticket under a chair at the station. she saw a worried man and asked if he had lost one. he said yes and told her about the ticket he needed. she checked that it was right before giving it back. he said thank you and put it away.
why did she check his answer first?
she wanted to make sure she was giving the ticket back to the right person.
did finding the ticket make it hers to keep?
no. she found it, but it was the ticket the man had lost.
what did the man do with it at the end?
he said thank you and put the ticket away.
i want three pieces of fruit from the market. my mother asks me to get two more for her. how many should i bring home?
five pieces of fruit: three for you and two for your mother.
my sister says she only wants one of my three. does that mean i need six?
not if she is taking one of the three already in your plan. you can still bring five, then give one of your three to your sister.
how many of those five are for me after that?
two are for you, two are for your mother, and one is for your sister.
now my mother says she only needs one after all. i have not bought anything yet.
then your plan can change to four pieces: two for you, one for your sister, and one for your mother.
why not five now?
because your mother changed her request from two to one before you bought the fruit. that makes the number of pieces one smaller.
make that explanation shorter.
you now need one less piece of fruit than before. you need four instead of five.
just give me the list for each person with no explanation.
two for you, one for your sister, and one for your mother.
i made soup for my friend, and she said it needed less salt. i feel as if she said i cannot cook.
her words were about the salt in this soup. that is different from saying you cannot cook at all.
i asked her what she thought of the taste, so i did want a real answer. i just felt sad when i heard it.
both can be true. you wanted useful information, and hearing it still felt hard. you can use what she said about salt without turning it into a rule about everything you make.
say the last part more simply.
you can use what she said about the salt without thinking that every meal you make is wrong.
what could i say to her?
thank you for telling me. i wanted to know what you thought. i will keep the salt in mind next time.
should i tell her she must like it because i worked on it?
you can tell her you put care into making it, but that does not mean she has to have the same taste as you.
please give me one short sentence to remember.
one answer about one meal is not a rule about all my cooking.
tell a story about someone who finds a simple way to remember where he stopped reading.

a boy read a little of his book after dinner each day. one evening, he put it down without leaving anything at the page to show where he stopped. the next day, he could not remember his place. he read a few lines he already knew, then found a new part. after that, he chose a small card to keep inside the book. each time he finished reading, he put the card at the place where he wanted to begin next time. the card did not remember the story for him, but it helped him find his place.
give me only the part about what he forgot to do that evening.
he put it down without leaving anything at the page to show where he stopped.
why did the card help?
it showed the place where he wanted to begin reading next time.
did the card teach him the meaning of the story?
no. it helped with finding a place in the book, not understanding the story.
what did he do before he began using the card?
he read a few lines he already knew and then found a new part.
write a sentence he could put on the card.
start reading here next time.
do you remember the walk we took together yesterday?
i do not take walks with people. if you mean a walk we talked about here, tell me which part you want to talk about.
use only our words. i mean i told you about a walk yesterday, but it was in another conversation.
i do not have that other conversation in front of me. if you tell me the important parts again, i can talk about them with you.
i walked to the park with my father. can you tell me what we saw?
not unless you give me those details. knowing that you walked with your father does not tell me what you saw along the way.
use the place i gave, but do not make up any other details.
you walked to the park with your father. you have not told me what you saw there.
we saw a woman drawing a tree. now ask me one question about that.
what did you like about the picture she was drawing?
i did not say i liked it.
you are right. a better question is: what did you think of the picture?
just give me that question.
what did you think of the picture?
my brother and i want to clean the kitchen together. he says i should wash the cups while he puts the books away. what else should we choose first?
you could choose which parts of the kitchen need work and what each person can finish. that helps keep one person from thinking the other will do everything else.
there are cups on the table, books on a chair, and food to put away.
then you already have a plan for the cups and books. you still need to choose who will put the food away, or whether you will do that part together.
he finishes with the books before i finish washing. does that mean he must take every other task?
not from the first plan alone. you can ask him to help with the food, but it is better to make that part clear rather than think he already knows.
make clear what we have chosen and what we have not chosen yet.
you chose a person for the cups and a person for the books. you have not yet chosen who will put the food away.
write a short question for my brother.
could you put the food away after the books, while i finish washing the cups?
what if he needs to leave early?
then ask what he has time to do and change the plan together.
which is better, a large book with empty pages or a small one?
what will you use it for? the better choice can change with what you need to write and where you will carry it.
i want to write short messages while i walk around town. i want something easy to carry.
a small one may work better for that. you said the writing will be short and that you want it to be easy to carry.
use book in the answer instead of one.
a small book may work better for your short messages because you want something easy to carry.
now i want to draw large pictures in it too. does that change the choice?
yes. large pictures may need more room on the page. you now have two needs to think about: easy carrying and enough space for drawing.
should you say the first answer was wrong all along?
no. the first answer used the needs you gave then. the new drawing need changes which parts of the choice we should think about.
use only words from the list and give me a short question about the choice.
which is more important for this book: space for large pictures or being easy to carry?
write this as if my sister is saying it herself: my sister left her book at home and went back to get it.
i left my book at home and went back to get it.
now say it as if i am telling someone about her.
my sister left her book at home and went back to get it.
what changed between those two sentences?
the person talking changed. the first has i and my because your sister is talking about herself. the other has my sister and her because you are talking about her.
give me the words about her that change between the two sentences.
my sister and her.
did the book move to a different place just because the words changed?
no. what happened stayed the same. only the way you talked about it changed.
what part of the meaning stayed the same?
your sister left her own book at home and went back to get it.
what if i write she left my book at home instead?
then my would make the book yours, not hers. that would change a fact about the book, not just who is talking.
i want my neighbor to water my plants while i am away. how can i ask without making it sound as if she has to say yes?
you could ask whether she has time and make clear that it is okay if she cannot. for example: would you have time to help with my plants while i am away? it is okay if that does not work for you.
i also need to say when i will be away.
yes. the time is important information for her choice. tell her which days you mean before asking her to choose an answer.
i will leave tomorrow and return the next evening. write the whole message.
i will be away from tomorrow until the next evening. would you have time to help with my plants while i am gone? it is okay if that does not work for you.
should i say she has said yes if she has not answered yet?
no. asking a question is not the same as getting a yes. wait for her answer before making it part of the plan.
use only our simple words for that last answer.
no. you asked, but she has not said yes. wait for her answer before making that your plan.
what if she says she can only help on one day?
then check whether that is enough for what you need. do not change her one day answer into a yes for both days.
write a story that stops with a person thinking about opening an old letter. do not tell me what is in the letter.

a woman was putting away books when she found an old letter she had written to herself. it was closed, with her name on the front. she remembered writing it after a long journey, but not the words inside. she sat by the window and held it for a while. outside, the light in the garden was changing. she thought about opening the letter, then looked at her own name again.
make the story shorter, but keep the last choice open.

a woman was putting away books when she found an old letter she had written to herself. it was closed, with her name on the front. she remembered writing it after a long journey, but not the words inside. she sat by the window and held it for a while. outside, the light in the garden was changing. she thought about opening the letter, then looked at her own name again.
why did you leave out the words inside?
you asked me not to tell you what was in the letter. the story can end with her choice still open.
does that make the story impossible to understand?
no. we know who found the letter and what choice she is thinking about. the words inside are simply not given.
the note says no food after the door is closed. is that a rule about where to eat or when to eat?
the words after the door is closed make it sound like a rule about time. the note says no food after that happens, but it does not clearly say which place the rule is for.
keep it simple and make the part about time clear.
it sounds like a rule about time. the note says no food after the door is closed. it does not clearly say which place the rule is for.
what should i ask the teacher?
you could ask: does the note mean we should finish eating before the door is closed, and which room is it about?
what if the note had said no food inside this room?
then it would be a rule about place. it would tell you not to eat in that room.
can you put the two ideas into one clear rule?
i would ask the teacher what she wants first. the first note does not give us enough information to put both ideas together without adding something new.
why would asking her help?
we need to know both when and where she wants the rule to be used. her answer could make that clear.
give me one reason why writing a list before going to the market can help.
a list can help you remember what you wanted to buy.
does that mean every list is useful?
no. a list could have the wrong things on it, or be too hard to read. being a list does not make it useful every time.
what would be an example where it does not help me remember?
if you leave the list at home and cannot remember what is on it, you may still need to work out what to buy at the market.
so should i never write a list?
that does not follow. a list can help when you have the right information and can use it. one example where it does not help is not a reason to say it can never help.
make that last answer shorter.
a list can still be useful, even though it does not help every time.
what if i write the list on my phone and take the phone?
then the list will be with you, if you keep it on the phone and can open it. you still need the things on the list to be what you really want to buy.
give me only the last sentence.
you still need the list to have the things you really want to buy.
my friend showed me a picture of an empty park. can i say nobody goes there at any time?
no. an empty park in one picture does not tell you that nobody goes there at any time. you only know that no person can be seen in that picture.
what if the picture was taken early in the morning?
that gives you more information about when it was taken. people could still visit at another time, and the picture would not tell you how often that happens.
i want to write only what i know from her picture.
you could say: the park looks empty in this picture.
can i say it is always quiet?
not from one picture. a picture does not give you the sound, and one moment does not show every part of every day.
i understand. ask me one useful question before helping me choose a time to visit.
what kind of visit would you like: a quiet walk, time with friends, or something else?
a quiet walk. do not give me a time you do not know.
i do not know when that park is most quiet. you could ask your friend what she knows about how busy it is in the morning, afternoon, or evening.
i finally put all my books on the shelf. just say something kind about that. do not ask me what i will do next.
that sounds like useful work finished. i hope you enjoy having the books where you want them.
i do. the desk feels much more open now.
it can feel good to see a space change after you have spent time on it.
can you make your reply sound more like a conversation between friends?
that sounds good. now you have more room to use your desk.
yes. give me another short reply like that.
nice. it sounds like your desk is ready for you again.
write a short line i could send my sister about it.
i finally put the books away, and my desk has room again.
add one question asking whether she wants the old small shelf.
i finally put the books away, and my desk has room again. would you like the old small shelf?
why can you add a question now if i said no questions at first?
your first request was about my reply to you then. you later asked for a message with a question for your sister.
